rationale: CORRECTED CASE (round-23 pre-seal amendment, .ufo/waves/round-23/preseal-amendment.md, written before any candidate was opened or measured). Same id and same scenario as the proposal cases-proposed/CaseTmpfsUsrquota.json, which is retained unaltered. Delta versus the proposal: the fixture's single btrfs_sysfs UUID record gains the amendment-required member qgroups_enabled (null), which the amendment pairs with qgroups=false and qgroups_mode=null ('qgroups false must pair with enabled=null/mode=null'); the mountinfo text, the paths entry, device_links and every expected value are unchanged. Re-derivation against the amendment's superseding C2 rules leaves the expectation identical: (1) Mount resolution — the amendment keeps longest component-prefix selection and adds 'if ANY covering mountpoint occurs more than once' => unknown/n/a/ambiguous_overmount with fstype=null, mount_point=null, device_check=not_checked; in this fixture the covering mountpoints for realpath '/dev/shm' are '/' (ext4 line) and '/dev/shm' (tmpfs line) and each occurs exactly once, so no ambiguity arises and the tmpfs line is still selected. Each line is parsed on its own with the separator and the last three fields (fstype, source, super options); the fixture's four lines carry no backslash escapes, so the 040/011/012/134 decode and the 'reject other backslash escapes' rule are not exercised, and the single trailing newline yields no non-empty trailing line. (2) Quota classification — the amendment's tmpfs rule preserves the keys quota, usrquota, grpquota and the four documented hardlimit options and states that an arbitrary '_hardlimit' suffix is NOT sufficient; this case uses the plain flag 'usrquota', which is a member of that preserved set, so the contract row 'tmpfs | any of quota,usrquota,grpquota or a key ending _hardlimit | enabled | enforced | tmpfs_quota_option' applies unchanged: quota_state=enabled, enforcement=enforced, basis=tmpfs_quota_option. 'enforced' here describes the mechanism flag, not a nonzero limit, and the fixture sets no limit at all; the amendment also notes the kernel normally emits an active quota flag alongside hardlimit options, which is precisely this shape. (3) Device check — the amendment makes device mismatch preempt the filesystem table (unknown/n/a/device_mismatch, device_check=mismatch) and skips the equality test for btrfs only when the stat major is 0; tmpfs is not btrfs, so the equality test applies, the tmpfs line's major:minor '0:26' equals the path's st_dev '0:26', and the row is not degraded. (4) Fixture shape — the amendment's path rules (nonempty, unique, normalized absolute path/realpath without dot/dotdot components; canonical decimal MAJ:MIN st_dev without signs or leading zeros except 0) hold for '/dev/shm' and '0:26'; UUID keys are canonical, device_links values are plain basenames without slashes or control characters; qgroups fields have exact bool/bool-or-null/mode-or-null types. (5) Verdict — no setup error, one path is enabled, so exit 1 and finding_id QUOTA_ENABLED, unchanged by the amendment, which preserves the six scored output fields. Source anchors, unchanged: S084 = Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst at v7.2, quota mount-option table 129-143 with the usrquota row at 135-136 ('User quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount.') and the mount-time-only note at 145; S082 = Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst §3.5 at v7.2, lines 1965-1990 with the field table at 1970-1983. Out-of-band realism check only (unregistered, not part of the derivation): upstream v7.2 mm/shmem.c has fsparam_flag("usrquota", Opt_usrquota) at 4462, case Opt_usrquota at 4626-4631 setting QTYPE_MASK_USR, and the superblock show_options emitting seq_printf(seq, ",usrquota") at 4878-4879 when sb_has_quota_active(root->d_sb, USRQUOTA), i.e. the kernel prints the bare key 'usrquota' into the mountinfo super-options column where the probe is told to read quota keys.
